analysis.title: "Boring Is Beautiful": BTIG Warns The Last Time This Happened Was 2000
key_insights: Over the past 30 days the S&P 500 Consumer Staples sector outperformed S&P Tech by 33%, the largest such move in roughly 25 years per BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky. The only comparable period was April 2000 through October 2001.

Krinsky is warming up to Consumer Staples. XLP has broken out of a multi-month base in absolute terms and versus the S&P 500 (XLP/SPX). He argues negative sentiment combined with strong price action is a powerful set-up, and the group is not particularly extended.
Cheap valuation has not protected investors this year. Goldman's memory-exposed basket (GSTMTMEM) is down 51% from its high even though memory names were considered cheap in June.

After the March 10, 2000 Nasdaq peak, staples gained 50.3%, utilities 44.0% and financials 36.4% over the next year, while tech fell 56.9% and the S&P fell 11.6%. Staples then beat tech by nearly 1,000bps over the following two years.

Since June 22, around the AI trade peak, healthcare is up 25.0%, energy 19.7% and staples 12.6%, while tech is down 7.3% and the S&P is up 0.6%. Krinsky notes the difference from 2000: many sectors were down 20-30% into the March 2000 peak, which did not happen this year.

The equal-weight staples vs discretionary ratio (RSPS/RSPD) has been basing for two years and closed Friday at 0.569. Krinsky says a breakout through .58 would have meaningful implications, but it is premature to call a new uptrend.

BofA's Hartnett disagrees: he lists mega-cap consumer stocks among the most vulnerable if the dollar and liquidity squeeze worsens, and lists discretionary among assets likely to surprise higher over the next eight weeks.
Tech (QQQ, SOXX) has fallen below its heaviest two-year volume-at-price zone, so rallies into it are likely to meet overhead supply. QQQ strong support is around $630, about 6% below the $674 close.
Krinsky thinks SOXX needs to retrace to its April breakout point, implying roughly 17-25% more downside from current levels.

Five constructive staples charts: COST (measured move target about $1300), MDLZ (breaking a downtrend that has capped rallies since 2023), CL (pressing the top of a multi-year base near $100), British American Tobacco (pre-breakout near 4,650p), and Brown-Forman BF/B (nearing breakout from a base held since mid-2025).

AAPL, up 31% YTD, hit a 52-week high and closed more than 1% below it on both Thursday and Friday. Over 20 years Krinsky found nine prior instances of this pattern, with 20-day returns negative 89% of the time (average -12.57%, median -8.97%). The sample is small and three cases overlap in early 2006. BTIG views AAPL as vulnerable to downside reversion.

The Bloomberg Dollar Index is breaking out of a two-year range, which Krinsky calls one of the most bullish charts he can find and probably not conducive to a risk-on environment. GBP, AUD, CAD and NZD are rolling over against the dollar. Goldman's FX team sees one more leg higher before a turn in 2027.

The article's author adds that staples are a bond proxy that broke out in a week when the 10Y closed at 5.15% and the market priced three more Fed hikes. The author reads the bid as a hiding place from an AI unwind. The author views the relative trade as right and the absolute one as a coin toss.

tension_points.bull_case: BTIG's Krinsky sees XLP breaking out in absolute and relative terms with bearish sentiment, and the 2000 analog had staples beating tech by nearly 1,000bps over the following two years.

tension_points.what_invalidates: A failure of the RSPS/RSPD ratio to break through .58, or a broad-based decline in which correlations rise toward one.
